document.title: Somewhere Statistical Soundness, Post-Quantum Security, and SNARGs

candidate.title: Somewhere Statistically Sound Arguments Are Fiat-Shamir Friendly
candidate.subtitle: A class that evades every known Fiat-Shamir counterexample -- conjecturally, for a reason
candidate.one_line: Any constant-round somewhere statistically sound interactive argument is Fiat-Shamir friendly.
candidate.status_note: Conjecture 1.3 of the source. It is explicit that it does not prove it, and asks for 'the proof (or refutation) of this conjecture' as an important open problem. It does prove that SSS implies straight-line soundness and hence post-quantum soundness, and that its own instantiation of Kilian's protocol is SSS.
candidate.progress_note: All known Fiat-Shamir counterexamples are for arguments that are not SSS, and the source explains structurally why: the extra accepting clause they rely on is precisely what destroys statistical soundness on any slice. The only argument previously proven Fiat-Shamir friendly is itself SSS.

candidate.why_interesting: It isolates exactly the class of arguments that dodges every known Fiat-Shamir counterexample, and a proof would be a step on a named route to SNARGs from a standard post-quantum assumption.
candidate.why_clean: One class, one transform, one existential quantifier over hash families.

quotes.quote: Conjecture 1.3. Any constant round SSS interactive argument (P, V) is Fiat-Shamir friendly.
We emphasize that we do not prove that any SSS interactive argument is Fiat-Shamir friendly, only conjecture it.
we conjecture that this instantiation is Fiat-Shamir friendly, and leave the proof (or refutation) of this conjecture as an important open problem.
meaning that for any SSS interactive argument (P, V) there exists a hash family H such that applying the Fiat-Shamir paradigm w.r.t. H to (P, V) results with a sound non-interactive argument.
We note that all known negative results for the Fiat-Shamir paradigm
prior to this work, the only interactive argument that was proven to be Fiat-Shamir friendly, in the work of Canetti et al.
we propose constructing an SSS interactive argument for all of NP as a great open problem.
Any θ-SSS interactive argument (P, V) w.r.t. a θ-decisional complexity assumption A is θ-straight-line sound.

check.notes: Conjecture 1.3 is verbatim on page 8 and the definition of Fiat-Shamir friendliness is quoted from the informal exposition on page 6. No repair was needed. One page correction: the 'proof (or refutation)' openness quote is on page 9, not page 7 as first recorded. The statement flags that the definition is existential in the hash family, since a reader could otherwise take the conjecture to be about Fiat-Shamir as deployed, which it is not.
